summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with shortness of breath, fatigue, and severe anemia (hemoglobin 7.5) following a recent rehabilitation stay after prior hospitalizations for sternal wound infection and C. difficile colitis. She presented with new exertional chest pain, orthopnea, and bilateral leg edema. Workup revealed heart failure exacerbation due to diastolic dysfunction and volume overload, likely compounded by chronic kidney disease. She was transfused two units of packed red blood cells, treated with IV furosemide which was transitioned to oral, and managed for hyperkalemia with kayexalate and dietary modification. Her C. difficile infection was ongoing, so oral vancomycin was continued and a taper plan was established. Blood pressure was optimized with adjustments to metoprolol, hydralazine, and addition of amlodipine. She improved clinically, with resolution of pulmonary edema on imaging, stable renal function, and better exercise tolerance. She was discharged to extended care with a plan for ongoing rehabilitation, medication management, and follow-up with cardiology and nephrology.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, hemiplegia affecting unspecified side
